title: Deliveries, Vehicles & Car Park Safety
blurb: Keeping people and moving vehicles apart in the car park and delivery areas, and handling deliveries and cages safely.
siteNotes: Where vehicles unload, the marked walkways and any banksman arrangements
Where the car park and delivery area are poorly lit or uneven
Which routes and ramps to treat with extra care with cages and trolleys
legalNotes: From BHB-10MT-59. Workplace transport is covered by the Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974 and the Workplace (Health, Safety and Welfare) Regulations 1992 (traffic routes); PPE under the Personal Protective Equipment at Work Regulations 1992; manual handling under the Manual Handling Operations Regulations 1992.

cards.title: Deliveries, Vehicles & Car Park Safety
cards.body:
By the end of this session you can:
- keep yourself away from moving vehicles
- stay visible and keep deliveries organised
- spot and report outdoor hazards

cards.title: People and vehicles mix
cards.body:
Our car park and delivery areas are busy places where people and vehicles mix: guest cars, delivery lorries, cellar drops and staff on foot.

Vehicles reversing or manoeuvring are a genuine hazard. Being aware and predictable around them keeps everyone safe.

cards.title: Keep people and vehicles apart
cards.body: The golden rule is to keep people and moving vehicles apart wherever possible.

items.title: Make eye contact
items.text: Before crossing behind or in front.

items.title: Do not assume
items.text: A reversing driver may not have seen you.

cards.title: Walkways and hi-vis
cards.body: Use marked walkways where they exist. Wear high-visibility clothing if you are working around vehicles in low light.

left.title: Do
items: Wear high-visibility clothing in low light

right.title: Do not
items: Assume the driver can see you

cards.title: Keep the area organised
cards.body:
During deliveries, keep the area organised. Agree where a vehicle will unload and keep routes clear.

Control cages and trolleys carefully. A loaded cage can be very heavy and hard to stop, especially on a slope or ramp, so never let one run away from you. Use good manual handling for offloading and do not rush.

items.title: Control the cage
items.text: Take care on slopes and ramps.

cards.title: Watch and flag
cards.body: Watch for hazards particular to outside areas. If you spot a problem, such as a blocked route, a reversing vehicle with no banksman or a dark corner, flag it.

cards.title: Remember
cards.body:
- Keep people and moving vehicles apart wherever possible
- Stay out of blind spots and never assume a driver has seen you
- Make eye contact before crossing near a vehicle
- Keep delivery routes clear and control cages and trolleys
- Flag blocked routes, dark corners and reversing with no one guiding

cards.q: What is the golden rule around moving vehicles?
options: Always wave drivers on when you see them
Keep people and moving vehicles apart wherever possible
Stand still when a vehicle moves near you
Walk quickly across the yard
cards.why: Keep people and moving vehicles apart wherever possible.

cards.q: You should never assume a reversing driver has seen you.
cards.why: Reversing drivers often cannot see you.

cards.q: Around vehicles in low light you should wear:
options: Dark clothing so you do not distract drivers
A coat with a hood to stay warm
High-visibility clothing
Nothing special if you are quick
cards.why: Wear high-visibility clothing if working around vehicles in low light.

cards.q: A loaded cage can be very hard to stop, especially on a slope.
cards.why: A loaded cage can be very heavy, so never let one run away from you.

cards.q: Before crossing near a vehicle, you should:
options: Make eye contact with the driver
Assume it has seen you
Wave and carry on walking
Hurry across while it is still
cards.why: Make eye contact with drivers before crossing behind or in front of them.

cards.q: You should stay out of drivers' blind spots.
cards.why: Drivers often cannot see you in their blind spots.

cards.q: Which is an outdoor hazard to watch for in the car park?
options: Ice in winter
Gravel being raked
The delivery driver's radio
A coat left on a chair
cards.why: Watch for uneven ground, ice in winter, poor lighting at night and reversing vehicles.

cards.q: During a delivery, routes should be kept clear.
cards.why: Agree where a vehicle will unload and keep routes clear.

cards.q: You spot a vehicle reversing with no one guiding it and a blocked route. You should:
options: Ignore it, as the driver will manage
Walk behind the vehicle to guide it
Flag it and report it
Carry on and cross quickly
cards.why: If you spot a problem, such as a reversing vehicle with no banksman or a blocked route, flag it.

cards.q: People and vehicles mixing is a genuine hazard in the car park.
cards.why: The car park and delivery areas are places where people and vehicles mix.
